from ui.system import _footer_font  # SYSTEM's copy: original file redefines it later, readers see the final object

def draw_menu_background():

    if bg_image:

        screen.blit(bg_image, (0, 0))

    else:

        screen.fill(C_BLACK)

def draw_menu():

    # ── Compute dt and advance all polish animation systems ──
    # Per PYGAME_MASTER_ENGINEER Module 4: dt-based motion so the feel is
    # identical at 60Hz, 144Hz, or under frame drops.
    now_ms = pygame.time.get_ticks()
    if not _anim.initialized:
        _init_menu_anim()
        _anim.last_ms = now_ms
    dt = (now_ms - _anim.last_ms) / 1000.0
    _anim.last_ms = now_ms
    # Clamp dt to a max of 1/15s so a long frame stall (window drag, etc.)
    # doesn't catapult rain drops across the screen.
    dt = min(dt, 1.0 / 15.0)
    _update_menu_anim(dt)

    # ── Detect mouse motion → release keyboard focus ──
    # If the mouse actually moved since last frame, hand control back to the
    # mouse. pygame.mouse.get_rel() returns the delta since the last call.
    mx, my = pygame.mouse.get_rel()
    if mx != 0 or my != 0:
        reset_keyboard_selection()

    # ── Background + rain + embers (under the dark panel) ──
    draw_menu_background()
    _draw_rain(screen)
    _draw_embers(screen)

    # Dark panel overlay (existing CRT-style left panel)
    screen.blit(_menu_overlay, (0, 0))

    # ── Top classification banner OR boot sequence ──
    # On first menu show, the boot banner plays a typewriter sequence.
    # Once done, the normal "// KRAPNET TERMINAL //" banner takes over.
    if not _draw_boot_banner(screen):
        classif_bar = pygame.Surface((460, 22), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        classif_bar.fill((8, 10, 14, 220))
        pygame.draw.line(classif_bar, C_ORANGE, (0, 0), (460, 0), 1)
        pygame.draw.line(classif_bar, C_ORANGE, (0, 21), (460, 21), 1)
        screen.blit(classif_bar, (20, 20))
        classif_text = _classification_font.render(
            "// KRAPNET TERMINAL - CLEARANCE: OPERATOR //", True, C_ORANGE
        )
        screen.blit(classif_text, (30, 24))

    # ── Title (no glow - kept clean per user preference) ──
    title_x = 40
    title_y = 110
    title_text = "CALL OF ACARISTAN"

    # Measure title for scanline math.
    title_surf = font_title.render(title_text, True, C_WHITE)
    title_w = title_surf.get_width()
    title_h = title_surf.get_height()

    # Drop shadow
    screen.blit(font_title.render(title_text, True, (0, 0, 0)),
                (title_x + 4, title_y + 4))
    # Main title
    screen.blit(title_surf, (title_x, title_y))

    # Scanline drift over the title text (drawn after, additive).
    _draw_scanline_drift(screen, title_x, title_y, title_w, title_h)

    # Orange accent bar under title
    pygame.draw.rect(screen, C_ORANGE, (title_x, title_y + 88, 320, 3))

    # ── Section header above menu buttons ──
    pygame.draw.line(screen, (60, 45, 25), (135, 320), (420, 320), 1)
    section_lbl = _classification_font.render("MAIN TERMINAL", True, (140, 100, 50))
    screen.blit(section_lbl, (135, 305))

    # ── Active save slot summary ──
    slot = save_system.get_slot()
    slot_idx = save_system.current_slot_index() + 1
    slot_panel = pygame.Surface((350, 48), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    slot_panel.fill((0, 0, 0, 135))
    pygame.draw.rect(slot_panel, (45, 70, 90, 120), slot_panel.get_rect(), 1)
    pygame.draw.line(slot_panel, C_KRAP_BLUE, (0, 0), (0, 48), 3)
    screen.blit(slot_panel, (135, 260))

    active = _footer_font.render(f"ACTIVE SAVE SLOT: {slot_idx}", True, (80, 150, 190))
    last = slot.get("last_completed_label", "No missions completed")
    if slot.get("last_completed_mission"):
        last = "LAST COMPLETED: " + last
    elif slot.get("occupied"):
        progress = slot.get("progress", "")
        if progress == "m1":
            last = "MISSION 1 IN PROGRESS"
        elif progress == "walk":
            last = "WALKING SIM IN PROGRESS"
        else:
            last = slot.get("last_completed_label", "Campaign started")
    else:
        last = "EMPTY SLOT - START A NEW CAMPAIGN"
    last_surf = _footer_font.render(last[:48], True, (145, 145, 135))
    screen.blit(active, (150, 268))
    screen.blit(last_surf, (150, 286))

    # ── Buttons ──
    has_save = save_system.has_any_save()
    if has_save:
        layout = [
            (0, 330, "CONTINUE"),
            (1, 390, "NEW CAMPAIGN"),
            (2, 450, "MULTIPLAYER"),
            (3, 510, "SETTINGS"),
            (4, 570, "EXIT"),
        ]
    else:
        # No Continue button until at least one save slot exists.
        layout = [
            (0, -999, "CONTINUE"),
            (1, 350, "NEW CAMPAIGN"),
            (2, 410, "MULTIPLAYER"),
            (3, 470, "SETTINGS"),
            (4, 530, "EXIT"),
        ]

    # Hide everything first, then place what the layout names. Without this a
    # button missing from the layout keeps the y it was last given, which means
    # it stays visible AND stays clickable at app.py's index - so forgetting an
    # entry here would leave a phantom row that fires some other button's
    # action. Now a forgotten entry simply does not appear.
    for btn in buttons:
        btn.y = -999
        btn.rect.y = -999

    for idx, y, text in layout:
        buttons[idx].text = text
        buttons[idx].y = y
        buttons[idx].rect.y = y

    for i, btn in enumerate(buttons):
        if btn.y < 0:
            btn.is_hovered = False
            btn.is_selected = False
            btn.update(dt)
            continue
        btn.check_hover(get_scaled_mouse())
        # Apply keyboard focus: a button is selected if its index matches
        # the keyboard cursor AND the mouse isn't currently hovering it.
        btn.is_selected = (_anim.keyboard_idx == i) and not btn.is_hovered
        btn.update(dt)
        btn.draw(screen)

    # ── News ticker (above footer) ──
    _draw_news_ticker(screen)

    # ── Bottom divider line above footer ──
    pygame.draw.line(screen, (40, 30, 15), (30, HEIGHT - 50), (470, HEIGHT - 50), 1)

    # ── Footer ──
    footer_left = _footer_font.render(
        "v0.1.0  ·  BUILD 4471", True, (90, 90, 95)
    )
    screen.blit(footer_left, (30, HEIGHT - 38))

    footer_right = _footer_font.render(
        "© RETARDOVICI INC.", True, (90, 90, 95)
    )
    screen.blit(footer_right, (470 - footer_right.get_width(), HEIGHT - 38))

    # Blinking status indicator
    if (pygame.time.get_ticks() // 600) % 2 == 0:
        pygame.draw.circle(screen, (50, 220, 100), (40, HEIGHT - 22), 3)
    else:
        pygame.draw.circle(screen, (30, 130, 60), (40, HEIGHT - 22), 3)

    status_text = _footer_font.render("CONNECTED - KRAPNET RELAY 7", True, (60, 70, 65))
    screen.blit(status_text, (50, HEIGHT - 26))

    # ── Vignette (drawn last so it darkens the edges over everything) ──
    _draw_vignette(screen)

    # NOTE: the custom arrow cursor is no longer drawn here. It moved to the
    # main loop (draw_menu_cursor, right after the state render pass) so it
    # also covers slot select / multiplayer / settings / pause / death / report
    # / notebook. Drawing it here too would double-blit it and double-apply its
    # additive hover glow.


# States that get the custom arrow instead of the OS pointer. Deliberately
# excludes:
#   GAME / WALK          - aiming states; they use the combat reticle instead
#   CUTSCENE / ESCAPE_CUTSCENE / BOOT_INTRO - cinematics and the studio bumper,
#                          where a pointer of any kind is out of place
# app.py hides the OS cursor on exactly these states (plus GAME/WALK), so the
# two lists must stay in step or you get either a double cursor or none.
CURSOR_ARROW_STATES = frozenset({
    "MENU", "SLOT_SELECT", "MULTIPLAYER", "SETTINGS", "SHOP", "BRIEFING",
    "PAUSED", "DEATH", "MISSION_COMPLETE", "NOTEBOOK_INSPECT",
})


def draw_menu_cursor(surface=None, state_name=None, suppressed=False):
    """Custom arrow cursor, replacing the OS pointer on every menu screen.

    Tactical pointer arrow (KRAP white, orange on hover) matching the
    menu's orange/white terminal language. Tip is the hotspot.

    Single call site: the main loop, after the state's own render pass (see
    app.py), so the arrow persists across slot select, multiplayer, settings,
    pause, death, mission report and notebook instead of only the main menu.

    *state_name* may be passed by the caller; when omitted it is read off the
    FSM. Screens outside _CURSOR_ARROW_STATES (gameplay, cutscenes, the boot
    bumper) get nothing - gameplay aims with a reticle and cinematics want no
    pointer at all.

    *suppressed* lets the caller force the arrow off for one frame while a
    state still nominally belongs to _CURSOR_ARROW_STATES. MULTIPLAYER is
    such a state: its panel wants the arrow, but once a match is live the
    arena draws the combat reticle and an arrow would stack on top of it.
    """
    if surface is None:
        surface = screen

    if suppressed:
        # Still consume the hover flag so a stale menu hover cannot leak into
        # the next menu frame while the match owns the pointer.
        consume_hover()
        return

    if state_name is None:
        import app as _app
        state_name = getattr(getattr(_app, "gsm", None), "current_name", "")
    if state_name not in CURSOR_ARROW_STATES:
        # Consume anyway so a stale hover can't leak into the next menu frame.
        consume_hover()
        return

    try:
        mx, my = get_scaled_mouse()
    except Exception:
        consume_hover()
        return

    # Shared flag: any ModernButton that reported a hover this frame, on any
    # screen. Falls back to the main-menu button list for callers that render
    # the arrow without the widget pass having run.
    hovered = consume_hover() or any(
        getattr(b, "is_hovered", False)
        for b in buttons
        if getattr(b, "y", -999) > 0
    )
    fill = C_ORANGE if hovered else C_WHITE
    # Arrow body: tip is the hotspot at (mx, my), tail extends down-right.
    pts = [
        (mx, my), (mx, my + 22), (mx + 5.5, my + 16.8),
        (mx + 8.8, my + 24), (mx + 11.4, my + 22.6),
        (mx + 8.2, my + 15.2), (mx + 13.6, my + 15.2),
    ]
    int_pts = [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in pts]
    if hovered:
        glow = pygame.Surface((44, 44), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        pygame.draw.circle(glow, (255, 120, 0, 50), (22, 22), 16)
        surface.blit(glow, (mx - 22, my - 22),
                     special_flags=pygame.BLEND_RGBA_ADD)
    # Soft drop shadow so the arrow survives bright bg art.
    shadow = [(x + 1, y + 2) for x, y in int_pts]
    pygame.draw.polygon(surface, (0, 0, 0), shadow)
    # Fill + crisp black edge + KRAP orange spine along the left edge.
    pygame.draw.polygon(surface, fill, int_pts)
    pygame.draw.polygon(surface, (0, 0, 0), int_pts, 2)
    pygame.draw.line(surface, C_ORANGE,
                     (mx + 1, my + 3), (mx + 1, my + 19), 1)


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MENU POLISH SYSTEMS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Applied per PYGAME_MASTER_ENGINEER Module 2 + Module 4:
#   - dt-based lerp for all motion (frame-rate independent)
#   - separate update() and draw() passes (MVC)
#   - pre-rendered surfaces for static art (vignette, glow sprites)
#
# Systems:
#   _lerp_dt          - frame-rate-independent lerp helper
#   _anim             - module-level state for all polish systems
#   _init_menu_anim   - populate rain drops + embers (idempotent)
#   _update_menu_anim - step all animations forward by dt seconds
#   _draw_rain        - 3-layer parallax rain + ground splashes
#   _draw_embers      - drifting fire embers from right-side glow
#   _draw_vignette    - radial dark edge overlay
#   _draw_title_glow  - pulsing orange halo behind the title
#   _draw_scanline_drift - moving horizontal scanline over the title
#   _draw_boot_banner - typewriter KRAPNET boot text on first menu show
#   _draw_news_ticker - scrolling lore ticker above the footer
#
# Keyboard navigation (Module 2 accessibility):
#   keyboard_idx                  - currently focused button index, -1 = mouse
#   handle_menu_keydown(event)    - call from acaristan MENU-state KEYDOWN
#   consume_keyboard_trigger()    - returns button index to fire, or -1
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════





# ── Module-level animation state ─────────────────────────────────────────
# All long-lived state for the polish systems lives here, initialized lazily
# on first draw_menu() call so we don't pay for it during gameplay.

class _MenuAnimState:
    """Holds all per-frame animation state for the menu polish systems.

    Kept as a plain class (not a dict) so attribute typos raise immediately.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.initialized = False
        self.last_ms = 0           # last pygame.time.get_ticks() value
        self.t = 0.0               # total elapsed time (seconds) since first draw
        self.rain_drops = []       # list of dicts: x, y, length, speed, layer, alpha
        self.splashes = []         # list of dicts: x, y, age, max_age, radius
        self.embers = []           # list of dicts: x, y, vx, vy, age, max_age, brightness
        self.vignette = None       # pre-rendered radial dark edge surface
        self.title_glow_pulse = 0.0  # 0..1, oscillates with sin(t * 1.8)
        self.boot_done = False
        self.boot_t = 0.0          # seconds since first menu draw
        self.boot_chars_typed = 0  # typewriter cursor for boot banner
        self.ticker_offset = 0.0   # pixels scrolled
        # Keyboard nav
        self.keyboard_idx = -1     # -1 = mouse control, 0..N-1 = focused button
        self.pending_trigger = -1  # button index that should fire this frame, or -1


_anim = _MenuAnimState()


# ── Boot sequence text ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Typewriter-rendered line-by-line in the classification banner area on the
# first menu show after launch. Each line appears with a small delay; once
# all lines are typed, the normal "// KRAPNET TERMINAL - CLEARANCE //
# banner takes over.
_BOOT_LINES = [
    "> KRAPNET TERMINAL v7.2.1",
    "> ESTABLISHING UPLINK ........ OK",
    "> AUTHENTICATING OPERATOR .... OK",
    "> CLEARANCE: OPERATOR",
    "> READY.",
]
_BOOT_LINE_DELAY = 0.18   # seconds between lines starting
_BOOT_CHAR_RATE  = 35.0   # chars per second


# ── News ticker messages ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Looping lore ticker that scrolls right-to-left above the footer. Each item
# is separated by a small orange diamond.
_TICKER_ITEMS = [
    "ROUTE 12 CHECKPOINT REMAINS UNDER KRAP CONTROL",
    "MAG SPOKESMAN DENIES INVOLVEMENT IN HIGHWAY BOMBING",
    "SEBY INVESTIGATION: NO NEW LEADS, SOURCES SAY",
    "IPA REINFORCEMENTS ARRIVING FROM THE NORTH - EXPECT DELAYS",
    "BIRIBEL TASKING ORDERS UPDATED - RELAY 7",
    "FUEGOTECH K1 LAUNCH PARTY INVITES LEAKED ONLINE",
    "WEATHER: HEAVY RAIN, VISIBILITY LOW - ALL ROUTES",
    "KRAP PUBLIC AFFAIRS: 'WE HAVE THE SITUATION IN HAND'",
]
_TICKER_SPEED = 60.0  # pixels per second


def _init_menu_anim():
    """Populate rain drops, embers, and pre-rendered surfaces.

    Idempotent - safe to call multiple times, only the first call does work.
    """
    if _anim.initialized:
        return
    _anim.initialized = True
    _anim.last_ms = pygame.time.get_ticks()

    # ---- Rain: 3 layers, very subtle ----
    # Tuned WAY down per user feedback ("pretty eh"). Now reads as a faint
    # atmospheric hint rather than a full storm - short streaks, dim alpha,
    # only 40 drops total across all three layers.
    layer_specs = [
        # (count, length_range, speed_range, alpha_range, thickness)
        (18, (6, 10),  (160, 240), (35, 60),   1),   # far - barely visible
        (15, (10, 16), (280, 380), (60, 90),   1),   # mid
        (7,  (16, 22), (440, 560), (90, 130),  1),   # near - slightly brighter
    ]
    for count, lr, sr, ar, thick in layer_specs:
        for _ in range(count):
            _anim.rain_drops.append({
                "x": _rng_legacy.uniform(0, WIDTH + 80),
                "y": _rng_legacy.uniform(0, HEIGHT),
                "length": _rng_legacy.uniform(*lr),
                "speed": _rng_legacy.uniform(*sr),
                "alpha": _rng_legacy.randint(*ar),
                "thickness": thick,
                # All drops share the same wind angle for visual coherence.
                "wind": -0.18,  # radians from vertical, blows slightly left
            })

    # ---- Vignette: pre-rendered radial gradient ----
    # Transparent in the center, dark at the edges. Built once and reused.
    vig = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    cx, cy = WIDTH // 2, HEIGHT // 2
    max_r = math.hypot(cx, cy)
    # Render as concentric rings from outside in - cheaper per-ring than
    # per-pixel, and the gradient is smooth enough at this resolution.
    for r in range(int(max_r), 0, -2):
        # 0 at center, 1 at edge.
        t = r / max_r
        # Ease so the darkening is concentrated near the edges.
        eased = t ** 2.2
        alpha = int(180 * eased)
        if alpha < 2:
            continue
        pygame.draw.circle(vig, (0, 0, 0, alpha), (cx, cy), r)
    _anim.vignette = vig


def _update_menu_anim(dt):
    """Advance all animation systems by dt seconds."""
    if not _anim.initialized:
        _init_menu_anim()

    _anim.t += dt
    _anim.title_glow_pulse = 0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(_anim.t * 1.8)

    # ---- Rain drops ----
    ground_y = int(HEIGHT * 0.88)
    for d in _anim.rain_drops:
        # Velocity vector: mostly downward, slight wind slant.
        vx = math.sin(d["wind"]) * d["speed"]
        vy = math.cos(d["wind"]) * d["speed"]
        d["x"] += vx * dt
        d["y"] += vy * dt
        # Wrap when off-screen.
        if d["y"] > ground_y:
            # Spawn a splash ripple on impact (rare, only mid/near layers
            # - kept sparse per "rain is pretty eh" feedback).
            if d["thickness"] >= 1 and _rng_legacy.random() < 0.12:
                _anim.splashes.append({
                    "x": d["x"],
                    "y": ground_y + _rng_legacy.uniform(0, 6),
                    "age": 0.0,
                    "max_age": _rng_legacy.uniform(0.35, 0.55),
                    "radius": _rng_legacy.uniform(3, 6),
                })
            d["y"] = _rng_legacy.uniform(-40, 0)
            d["x"] = _rng_legacy.uniform(-40, WIDTH + 80)
        elif d["x"] < -50:
            d["x"] = WIDTH + 40

    # ---- Splashes ----
    # Cheap pooled list - remove in place by swapping with the last element.
    i = 0
    while i < len(_anim.splashes):
        s = _anim.splashes[i]
        s["age"] += dt
        if s["age"] >= s["max_age"]:
            _anim.splashes[i] = _anim.splashes[-1]
            _anim.splashes.pop()
        else:
            i += 1

    # ---- Embers ----
    # Spawn new embers from the right edge (where the bg fire glow lives).
    # Rate scales with dt so spawn density is frame-rate independent.
    spawn_chance = 60.0 * dt  # avg 60 per second
    while spawn_chance > 0:
        if _rng_legacy.random() < min(1.0, spawn_chance):
            _anim.embers.append({
                "x": _rng_legacy.uniform(WIDTH - 80, WIDTH + 10),
                "y": _rng_legacy.uniform(HEIGHT * 0.45, HEIGHT * 0.85),
                "vx": _rng_legacy.uniform(-1.5, -0.4),
                "vy": _rng_legacy.uniform(-1.2, -0.2),
                "age": 0.0,
                "max_age": _rng_legacy.uniform(2.0, 4.0),
                "brightness": _rng_legacy.uniform(0.6, 1.0),
                "size": _rng_legacy.randint(1, 2),
            })
        spawn_chance -= 1.0

    i = 0
    while i < len(_anim.embers):
        e = _anim.embers[i]
        e["age"] += dt
        e["x"] += e["vx"]
        e["y"] += e["vy"]
        # Slight upward acceleration as the ember heats.
        e["vy"] -= 0.02 * dt * 60
        if e["age"] >= e["max_age"] or e["x"] < -10 or e["y"] < -10:
            _anim.embers[i] = _anim.embers[-1]
            _anim.embers.pop()
        else:
            i += 1

    # ---- Boot sequence ----
    if not _anim.boot_done:
        _anim.boot_t += dt
        # Total chars across all lines + delays between lines.
        total_chars = sum(len(line) for line in _BOOT_LINES)
        total_delays = _BOOT_LINE_DELAY * len(_BOOT_LINES)
        total_duration = total_chars / _BOOT_CHAR_RATE + total_delays
        _anim.boot_chars_typed = int(
            max(0.0, _anim.boot_t) * _BOOT_CHAR_RATE
        )
        if _anim.boot_t >= total_duration + 0.4:
            _anim.boot_done = True

    # ---- News ticker ----
    _anim.ticker_offset += _TICKER_SPEED * dt
    # Wrap when we've scrolled one full loop width.
    # Computed lazily in _draw_news_ticker; just keep the offset bounded.
    if _anim.ticker_offset > 10_000:
        _anim.ticker_offset -= 10_000


# ── Draw helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _draw_rain(surface):
    """3-layer parallax rain + ground splashes."""
    if not _anim.initialized:
        return
    # Single scratch surface for all drops - drawn once per frame, cheaper
    # than per-drop SRCALPHA surfaces.
    rain_surf = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    for d in _anim.rain_drops:
        vx = math.sin(d["wind"])
        vy = math.cos(d["wind"])
        x2 = d["x"] + vx * d["length"]
        y2 = d["y"] + vy * d["length"]
        col = (180, 200, 220, d["alpha"])
        if d["thickness"] == 1:
            pygame.draw.line(rain_surf, col,
                             (int(d["x"]), int(d["y"])),
                             (int(x2), int(y2)), 1)
        else:
            pygame.draw.line(rain_surf, col,
                             (int(d["x"]), int(d["y"])),
                             (int(x2), int(y2)), 2)
    surface.blit(rain_surf, (0, 0))

    # Splashes on top of rain.
    if _anim.splashes:
        splash_surf = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        for s in _anim.splashes:
            t = s["age"] / s["max_age"]
            r = int(s["radius"] * (1 + t * 3))
            a = int(180 * (1 - t))
            if a <= 0 or r <= 0:
                continue
            pygame.draw.ellipse(
                splash_surf, (180, 200, 220, a),
                (int(s["x"] - r), int(s["y"] - r // 2), r * 2, r),
                1,
            )
        surface.blit(splash_surf, (0, 0))


def _draw_embers(surface):
    """Drifting fire embers from the right-side bg glow."""
    if not _anim.initialized or not _anim.embers:
        return
    em_surf = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    for e in _anim.embers:
        t = e["age"] / e["max_age"]
        # Brightness fades in then out.
        fade = math.sin(t * math.pi) * e["brightness"]
        if fade <= 0:
            continue
        # Color: bright yellow at birth → orange mid → red at death.
        if t < 0.4:
            col = (255, int(180 + 60 * (1 - t / 0.4)), 80, int(220 * fade))
        elif t < 0.75:
            col = (255, 130, 40, int(220 * fade))
        else:
            col = (220, 80, 30, int(180 * fade))
        r = e["size"]
        pygame.draw.circle(em_surf, col, (int(e["x"]), int(e["y"])), r)
        # Soft halo around bright embers.
        if fade > 0.5:
            halo_a = int(60 * fade)
            pygame.draw.circle(
                em_surf, (255, 140, 60, halo_a),
                (int(e["x"]), int(e["y"])), r * 2, 1
            )
    surface.blit(em_surf, (0, 0))


def _draw_vignette(surface):
    """Pre-rendered radial dark edge overlay."""
    if _anim.vignette is not None:
        surface.blit(_anim.vignette, (0, 0))


def _draw_title_glow(surface, title_x, title_y, title_w, title_h):
    """Slow orange glow pulse behind the title."""
    if not _anim.initialized:
        return
    # Glow size covers the title plus a 40px margin.
    glow_w = title_w + 80
    glow_h = title_h + 60
    glow = pygame.Surface((glow_w, glow_h), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    cx, cy = glow_w // 2, glow_h // 2
    max_r = math.hypot(cx, cy)
    pulse = _anim.title_glow_pulse
    # Layered concentric ellipses, each softer than the last.
    for r in range(int(max_r), 4, -8):
        t = r / max_r
        eased = (1 - t) ** 2
        alpha = int(45 * eased * pulse)
        if alpha < 2:
            continue
        pygame.draw.ellipse(
            glow, (255, 120, 0, alpha),
            (cx - r, cy - int(r * 0.55), r * 2, int(r * 1.1))
        )
    surface.blit(
        glow,
        (title_x + title_w // 2 - glow_w // 2,
         title_y + title_h // 2 - glow_h // 2),
        special_flags=pygame.BLEND_RGBA_ADD,
    )


def _draw_scanline_drift(surface, x, y, w, h):
    """A bright horizontal scanline that slowly drifts across the title."""
    if not _anim.initialized:
        return
    # Drift period: 5 seconds top-to-bottom.
    period = 5.0
    t = (_anim.t % period) / period
    line_y = y + int(t * h)
    # Bright line + soft glow above/below.
    line_surf = pygame.Surface((w, 12), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    for i in range(12):
        a = int(80 * (1 - abs(i - 6) / 6))
        if a > 0:
            pygame.draw.line(line_surf, (255, 200, 140, a),
                             (0, i), (w, i), 1)
    surface.blit(line_surf, (x, line_y - 6),
                 special_flags=pygame.BLEND_RGBA_ADD)


def _draw_boot_banner(surface):
    """Typewriter KRAPNET boot sequence shown on first menu show.

    Returns True while the boot is still playing (so draw_menu can suppress
    the normal classification banner), False when done.
    """
    if _anim.boot_done:
        return False

    # Backdrop - same dimensions as the normal classification banner.
    banner = pygame.Surface((460, 22), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    banner.fill((8, 10, 14, 230))
    pygame.draw.line(banner, C_ORANGE, (0, 0), (460, 0), 1)
    pygame.draw.line(banner, C_ORANGE, (0, 21), (460, 21), 1)
    surface.blit(banner, (20, 20))

    # Render lines with a typewriter effect, staggered by _BOOT_LINE_DELAY.
    chars_remaining = _anim.boot_chars_typed
    y_offset = 24
    for line_idx, line in enumerate(_BOOT_LINES):
        # Each line starts typing at line_idx * _BOOT_LINE_DELAY worth of
        # chars consumed.
        start_chars = int(line_idx * _BOOT_LINE_DELAY * _BOOT_CHAR_RATE)
        if chars_remaining <= start_chars:
            break
        chars_on_this_line = min(
            len(line), chars_remaining - start_chars
        )
        visible = line[:chars_on_this_line]
        # Blinking cursor on the line currently being typed.
        if chars_on_this_line < len(line) and \
           (line_idx == len(_BOOT_LINES) - 1 or
            chars_remaining < start_chars + len(line)):
            if int(_anim.t * 3) % 2 == 0:
                visible += "_"
        surf = _classification_font.render(visible, True, C_ORANGE)
        surface.blit(surf, (30, y_offset))
        y_offset += 14
        if y_offset > 64:  # clamp to banner area
            break

    return True


def _draw_news_ticker(surface):
    """Scrolling lore ticker above the footer."""
    # Compose the full ticker string with separators.
    # ASCII separator: "◆" is tofu on the bundled font, so never render it.
    separator = " // "
    full = separator.join(_TICKER_ITEMS) + separator
    full_surf = _footer_font.render(full, True, (180, 160, 110))
    sep_surf = _footer_font.render(separator, True, C_ORANGE)
    sep_w = sep_surf.get_width()
    full_w = full_surf.get_width()

    # Ticker area: above the footer divider line, full width of the dark panel.
    ticker_y = HEIGHT - 56
    ticker_h = 18
    # Backdrop strip.
    strip = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, ticker_h), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    strip.fill((0, 0, 0, 150))
    surface.blit(strip, (0, ticker_y))

    # KRAPNET WIRE label on the left - static.
    label = _classification_font.render("KRAPNET WIRE", True, C_ORANGE)
    label_w = label.get_width() + 16
    surface.blit(label, (8, ticker_y + 2))
    # Vertical separator after the label.
    pygame.draw.line(surface, (90, 60, 25),
                     (label_w, ticker_y),
                     (label_w, ticker_y + ticker_h), 1)

    # Scrolling text window: from label_w to WIDTH.
    window_w = WIDTH - label_w - 4
    if window_w <= 0 or full_w <= 0:
        return

    # Offset wraps modulo (full_w + sep_w) so the loop is seamless.
    period = full_w + sep_w
    offset = int(_anim.ticker_offset) % period

    # Draw the text twice - once at -offset, once at (period - offset) - so
    # the loop has no visible gap when it wraps.
    clip_rect = pygame.Rect(label_w + 2, ticker_y, window_w, ticker_h)
    prev_clip = surface.get_clip()
    surface.set_clip(clip_rect)
    surface.blit(full_surf, (label_w + 4 - offset, ticker_y + 2))
    surface.blit(full_surf, (label_w + 4 - offset + period, ticker_y + 2))
    surface.set_clip(prev_clip)

    # Top border line on the ticker strip.
    pygame.draw.line(surface, (60, 40, 15),
                     (0, ticker_y), (WIDTH, ticker_y), 1)


# ── Keyboard navigation API ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Public functions called by acaristan.py. Designed so the existing mouse
# click path keeps working unchanged - keyboard input is layered on top.


def _visible_button_indices():
    """Return list of indices into `buttons[]` that are currently on-screen.

    draw_menu() sets each button's `y` to -999 when it should be hidden
    (e.g. CONTINUE when no save exists). We respect that convention here.
    """
    return [i for i, b in enumerate(buttons) if b.y > 0]


def handle_menu_keydown(event):
    """Process a KEYDOWN event in the MENU state.

    Call from acaristan.py's event loop when game_state == "MENU".
    Returns None - side effects are stored in _anim.pending_trigger, which
    acaristan.py reads via consume_keyboard_trigger().
    """
    if not _anim.initialized:
        _init_menu_anim()

    if event.key in (pygame.K_UP, pygame.K_w):
        visible = _visible_button_indices()
        if not visible:
            return
        if _anim.keyboard_idx == -1:
            # Initializing from mouse control - pick the bottom visible.
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[-1]
        elif _anim.keyboard_idx in visible:
            i = visible.index(_anim.keyboard_idx)
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[(i - 1) % len(visible)]
        else:
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[-1]
        audio.play("menu_hover", volume=0.3)
    elif event.key in (pygame.K_DOWN, pygame.K_s):
        visible = _visible_button_indices()
        if not visible:
            return
        if _anim.keyboard_idx == -1:
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[0]
        elif _anim.keyboard_idx in visible:
            i = visible.index(_anim.keyboard_idx)
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[(i + 1) % len(visible)]
        else:
            _anim.keyboard_idx = visible[0]
        audio.play("menu_hover", volume=0.3)
    elif event.key in (pygame.K_RETURN, pygame.K_SPACE):
        if _anim.keyboard_idx != -1:
            _anim.pending_trigger = _anim.keyboard_idx
            buttons[_anim.keyboard_idx].press()
            audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.5)


def consume_keyboard_trigger():
    """Return the button index that should fire this frame, or -1.

    acaristan.py should call this after draw_menu() and route the trigger
    through the same action handlers as a mouse click.
    """
    t = _anim.pending_trigger
    _anim.pending_trigger = -1
    return t


def reset_keyboard_selection():
    """Clear keyboard focus - called when the mouse moves."""
    _anim.keyboard_idx = -1

# ── Panel geometry ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# The panel is split into three horizontal bands, all derived from
# these two numbers so nothing can drift out of alignment:
#
#   header : panel top .. SERVER_LIST_TOP
#   body   : SERVER_LIST_TOP .. SERVER_LIST_LIMIT  (list / chat)
#   footer : SERVER_FOOTER_TOP .. panel bottom     (actions)
#
# The old layout had one 184px header and no footer band at all, so
# the last visible server row was drawn underneath the BACK button
# and the scroll hint landed past the panel's own content area.

SERVER_PANEL_W = 940

SERVER_PANEL_H = 620

SERVER_PANEL_X = (WIDTH - SERVER_PANEL_W) // 2

SERVER_PANEL_Y = (HEIGHT - SERVER_PANEL_H) // 2

SERVER_HEADER_Y = SERVER_PANEL_Y + 22

# The subtitle hangs off the *measured* title height, not a magic
# offset - a font fallback (no Impact) must not re-collide them.

SERVER_SUBTITLE_Y = SERVER_PANEL_Y + 80

SERVER_CONNECT_Y = max(
    SERVER_PANEL_Y + 105,
    SERVER_SUBTITLE_Y + font_terminal_small.get_height() + 8,
)

SERVER_TAB_Y = SERVER_CONNECT_Y + 35

SERVER_DIVIDER_Y = SERVER_TAB_Y + 38

# Server list lives on the LEFT side of the panel

SERVER_ROW_X = SERVER_PANEL_X + 34

SERVER_ROW_W = 580

SERVER_LIST_TOP = max(SERVER_PANEL_Y + 210, SERVER_DIVIDER_Y + 36)

# Footer band: divider, BACK button and the ESC hint live here.

SERVER_FOOTER_TOP = SERVER_PANEL_Y + SERVER_PANEL_H - 76

SERVER_BACK_Y = SERVER_FOOTER_TOP + 12

# Hard ceiling for list content - no row is ever drawn past this,
# whatever the font metrics turn out to be.

SERVER_LIST_LIMIT = SERVER_FOOTER_TOP - 26

# font_terminal renders a 28px tall glyph box, so a 2-line name needs
# 28px of leading to stop the boxes touching (the old 20px leading
# overlapped them by 8px).  6 + 28 + 28 = 62, which is what a 70px row
# can carry with 4px to spare.

SERVER_ROW_LEAD = 28

SERVER_ROW_H_SINGLE = 46

SERVER_ROW_H_DOUBLE = 70

SERVER_ROW_GAP = 6

# A 2-line name plus its region line never fitted in 64px, so the
# region moved into the hover tooltip. These heights always fit
# between SERVER_LIST_TOP and SERVER_LIST_LIMIT.

SERVER_VISIBLE_ROWS = 4

SERVER_NAME_MAX_W = 322 - 24

SERVER_BADGE_W = 78

# Right-hand columns. 580px of row minus the widest possible values
# ("99/100" = 78px, "400ms" = 65px) leaves >=12px between each.

SERVER_STATUS_X = SERVER_ROW_X + 322

SERVER_PLAYERS_X = SERVER_ROW_X + 414

SERVER_PING_X = SERVER_ROW_X + 504

# Chat panel lives on the RIGHT side, sharing the body's bottom edge

CHAT_PANEL_X = SERVER_PANEL_X + SERVER_PANEL_W - 270

CHAT_PANEL_Y = SERVER_LIST_TOP

CHAT_PANEL_W = 240

CHAT_PANEL_H = SERVER_LIST_LIMIT - CHAT_PANEL_Y

# Contacts list (CONNECTIONS tab)

CONTACTS_X = SERVER_PANEL_X + 28

CONTACTS_Y = SERVER_LIST_TOP - 4

CONTACTS_W = 400

CONNECTIONS_ROW_H = 40

_chat_messages = []

_chat_next_spawn = 0

_server_animation_timer = 0

_refresh_active = False

_refresh_progress = 0.0

_scroll_offset = 0

refresh_btn_rect = pygame.Rect(SERVER_PANEL_X + SERVER_PANEL_W - 110, SERVER_CONNECT_Y, 82, 26)

kick_dismiss_btn_rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 160, 30)

def _server_status(cur, max_p, ping):

    if cur >= max_p:

        return "FULL", (220, 120, 45)

    if ping >= 180:

        return "UNSTABLE", (220, 80, 70)

    return "OPEN", C_TERMINAL

def _draw_server_badge(text, color, x, y, w=78):

    badge = pygame.Surface((w, 22), pygame.SRCALPHA)

    badge.fill((8, 12, 16, 210))

    pygame.draw.rect(badge, color, badge.get_rect(), 1)

    screen.blit(badge, (x, y))

    label = font_terminal_small.render(text, True, color)

    screen.blit(label, (x + w // 2 - label.get_width() // 2, y + 4))

def _fit_text(text, font, max_width):

    if font.size(text)[0] <= max_width:

        return text

    ellipsis = "..."

    while text and font.size(text + ellipsis)[0] > max_width:

        text = text[:-1]

    return text + ellipsis

def update_server_browser_animation():

    """Called once per frame while on multiplayer screen."""

    global _server_animation_timer, _chat_next_spawn, _chat_messages

    global _refresh_active, _refresh_progress

    # Pull the latest relay snapshot FIRST, so the ping jitter and chat
    # spawner below operate on current data rather than last frame's.

    _sync_relay_into_server_list()

    _server_animation_timer += 1

    # Animate pings + player counts every ~90 frames (1.5s).
    # Skipped when a live relay is driving the list: those numbers are
    # authoritative, and jittering them would be a lie.

    if relay_is_live():

        pass

    elif _server_animation_timer % 90 == 0 and not _refresh_active:

        for i, (name, cur, max_p, ping) in enumerate(server_list):

            delta = _rng_legacy.choice([-1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1])

            new_cur = max(0, min(max_p, cur + delta))

            new_ping = max(8, min(400, ping + _rng_legacy.randint(-6, 6)))

            server_list[i] = (name, new_cur, max_p, new_ping)

    # Refresh progress

    if _refresh_active:

        _refresh_progress += 0.025

        if _refresh_progress >= 1.0:

            _refresh_active = False

            _refresh_progress = 0.0

            for i, (name, cur, max_p, ping) in enumerate(server_list):

                new_cur = max(0, min(max_p, cur + _rng_legacy.randint(-3, 3)))

                new_ping = max(8, min(400, ping + _rng_legacy.randint(-25, 25)))

                server_list[i] = (name, new_cur, max_p, new_ping)

    # Spawn chat messages.
    # Suppressed while a live relay is connected: real players' lines are
    # arriving over the socket, and mixing in CHAT_POOL fiction would make
    # it impossible to tell who is actually in the lobby.

    if not relay_is_live():

        _chat_next_spawn -= 1

    if not relay_is_live() and _chat_next_spawn <= 0:

        msg = _rng_legacy.choice(CHAT_POOL)

        _chat_messages.append({

            "user": msg[0],

            "text": msg[1],

            "color": msg[2],

            "age": 0,

            # Marks this line as invented, so the handover to a live relay
            # can drop fiction without touching real players' messages.

            "fict": True,

        })

        _chat_next_spawn = _rng_legacy.randint(60, 130)

        if _rng_legacy.random() < 0.18:

            msg2 = _rng_legacy.choice(CHAT_POOL)

            _chat_messages.append({

                "user": msg2[0],

                "text": msg2[1],

                "color": msg2[2],

                "age": 0,

                "fict": True,

            })

        if len(_chat_messages) > 50:

            _chat_messages.pop(0)

    # Age messages

    for m in _chat_messages:

        m["age"] += 1

def switch_mp_tab(tab):

    global _mp_tab

    _mp_tab = tab

    audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.3)

def open_dm(user_idx):

    global _dm_open_user, _dm_input

    _dm_open_user = user_idx

    _dm_input = ""

    if user_idx not in _dm_history:

        _dm_history[user_idx] = []

    audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.3)

def close_dm():

    global _dm_open_user, _dm_input

    _dm_open_user = None

    _dm_input = ""

def send_dm_message():

    global _dm_input, _dm_response_delay, _dm_pending_reply

    if _dm_open_user is None or not _dm_input.strip():

        return

    _dm_history[_dm_open_user].append({

        "from": "you",

        "text": _dm_input.strip(),

        "age": 0,

    })

    _dm_input = ""

    _dm_response_delay = _rng_legacy.randint(45, 110)

    _dm_pending_reply = _dm_open_user

    audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.2)

def update_dm_state():

    global _dm_response_delay, _dm_pending_reply

    if _dm_open_user is not None and _dm_open_user in _dm_history:

        for m in _dm_history[_dm_open_user]:

            m["age"] += 1

    if _dm_response_delay > 0:

        _dm_response_delay -= 1

        if _dm_response_delay == 0 and _dm_pending_reply is not None:

            reply = _rng_legacy.choice(CONNECTIONS[_dm_pending_reply]["replies"])

            _dm_history[_dm_pending_reply].append({

                "from": "them",

                "text": reply,

                "age": 0,

            })

            _dm_pending_reply = None

            audio.play("menu_hover", volume=0.3)

def _status_color(status):

    if "Online" in status or status == "always":

        return (80, 220, 100)

    if "Away" in status or "Meeting" in status:

        return (220, 180, 60)

    if "Game" in status:

        return (100, 160, 220)

    if "Offline" in status or "Deleted" in status or "never" in status:

        return (110, 110, 110)

    if "\u2588" in status:

        return (140, 60, 60)

    return (180, 180, 180)

def draw_connections_panel():

    """Draws the friends list + active DM window."""

    mouse_pos = get_scaled_mouse()

    list_x = CONTACTS_X

    list_y = CONTACTS_Y

    list_w = CONTACTS_W

    row_h = CONNECTIONS_ROW_H

    list_header = font_terminal_small.render("CONTACTS", True, (80, 130, 160))

    screen.blit(list_header, (list_x + 6, list_y - 20))

    online_count = sum(1 for c in CONNECTIONS if "Online" in c["status"])

    online_lbl = font_terminal_small.render(

        f"{online_count} ONLINE  \u00b7  {len(CONNECTIONS)} TOTAL",

        True, (90, 130, 100),

    )

    screen.blit(online_lbl, (list_x + list_w - online_lbl.get_width() - 6, list_y - 20))

    list_bottom_limit = SERVER_LIST_LIMIT

    visible_friends = (list_bottom_limit - list_y) // row_h

    visible_friends = min(visible_friends, len(CONNECTIONS))

    for vi in range(visible_friends):

        i = vi + _dm_scroll_offset

        if i >= len(CONNECTIONS):

            break

        conn = CONNECTIONS[i]

        ry = list_y + vi * row_h

        row_rect = pygame.Rect(list_x, ry, list_w, row_h - 4)

        hover = row_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos)

        is_open = _dm_open_user == i

        row_surf = pygame.Surface((list_w, row_h - 4), pygame.SRCALPHA)

        if is_open:

            row_surf.fill((28, 36, 42, 235))

            pygame.draw.rect(row_surf, C_ORANGE, row_surf.get_rect(), 1)

            pygame.draw.rect(row_surf, (255, 120, 0, 130), (0, 0, 3, row_h - 4))

        elif hover:

            row_surf.fill((18, 28, 34, 225))

            pygame.draw.rect(row_surf, (80, 120, 140), row_surf.get_rect(), 1)

        else:

            row_surf.fill((9, 14, 18, 210))

            pygame.draw.rect(row_surf, (28, 44, 56), row_surf.get_rect(), 1)

        screen.blit(row_surf, row_rect)

        s_col = _status_color(conn["status"])

        pygame.draw.circle(screen, s_col, (list_x + 14, ry + row_h // 2 - 2), 4)

        name_col = C_WHITE if (hover or is_open) else conn["color"]

        name_surf = font_terminal.render(conn["name"], True, name_col)

        screen.blit(name_surf, (list_x + 28, ry + 4))

        # One line per contact: name left, status right-aligned. It used to
        # be a second line under a 34px-tall row, so it spilled out of the
        # row and into the contact below. The name is the identity here, so
        # the status is the half that gets the ellipsis.
        status_text = f"{conn['status']}  \u00b7  {conn['last_seen']}"

        status_w = list_w - 28 - 8 - name_surf.get_width() - 16

        status_surf = font_terminal_small.render(_fit_text(status_text, font_terminal_small, max(48, status_w)), True, (120, 130, 140))

        screen.blit(status_surf, (list_x + list_w - 8 - status_surf.get_width(), ry + 8))

    # ── Scroll indicators ──

    remaining_below = len(CONNECTIONS) - (_dm_scroll_offset + visible_friends)

    remaining_above = _dm_scroll_offset

    more_y = list_y + visible_friends * row_h + 4

    if remaining_below > 0 and remaining_above > 0:

        more_lbl = font_terminal_small.render(

            f"\u2191 {remaining_above} above  \u00b7  \u2193 {remaining_below} below  \u00b7  scroll wheel",

            True, (90, 110, 130),

        )

        screen.blit(more_lbl, (list_x + 6, more_y))

    elif remaining_below > 0:

        more_lbl = font_terminal_small.render(

            f"\u2193 {remaining_below} more contacts  \u00b7  scroll wheel",

            True, (90, 110, 130),

        )

        screen.blit(more_lbl, (list_x + 6, more_y))

    elif remaining_above > 0:

        more_lbl = font_terminal_small.render(

            f"\u2191 {remaining_above} above  \u00b7  scroll wheel",

            True, (90, 110, 130),

        )

        screen.blit(more_lbl, (list_x + 6, more_y))

    # ── Scrollbar for contacts ──

    if len(CONNECTIONS) > visible_friends:

        sb_x = list_x + list_w + 4

        sb_y = list_y

        sb_h = visible_friends * row_h - 4

        sb_w = 5

        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (15, 22, 28), (sb_x, sb_y, sb_w, sb_h))

        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (28, 44, 56), (sb_x, sb_y, sb_w, sb_h), 1)

        thumb_ratio = visible_friends / len(CONNECTIONS)

        thumb_h = max(20, int(sb_h * thumb_ratio))

        max_scroll = max(1, len(CONNECTIONS) - visible_friends)

        thumb_y = sb_y + int((sb_h - thumb_h) * (_dm_scroll_offset / max_scroll))

        pygame.draw.rect(screen, C_ORANGE, (sb_x, thumb_y, sb_w, thumb_h))

    # DM window (right column)

    dm_x = list_x + list_w + 16

    dm_y = list_y - 4

    dm_w = SERVER_PANEL_X + SERVER_PANEL_W - dm_x - 28

    # Stopped above the footer divider, which used to clip the send hint.

    dm_h = SERVER_LIST_LIMIT - 8 - dm_y

    dm_bg = pygame.Surface((dm_w, dm_h), pygame.SRCALPHA)

    dm_bg.fill((6, 11, 16, 230))

    pygame.draw.rect(dm_bg, (30, 50, 60), dm_bg.get_rect(), 1)

    pygame.draw.rect(dm_bg, (40, 60, 70, 100), dm_bg.get_rect(), 1)

    screen.blit(dm_bg, (dm_x, dm_y))

    if _dm_open_user is None:

        empty_lbl = font_terminal.render("// SELECT A CONTACT //", True, (60, 90, 110))

        screen.blit(

            empty_lbl,

            (dm_x + dm_w // 2 - empty_lbl.get_width() // 2,

             dm_y + dm_h // 2 - 20),

        )

        hint = font_terminal_small.render(

            "Click a name on the left to start a conversation",

            True, (50, 70, 85),

        )

        screen.blit(

            hint,

            (dm_x + dm_w // 2 - hint.get_width() // 2,

             dm_y + dm_h // 2 + 8),

        )

    else:

        conn = CONNECTIONS[_dm_open_user]

        s_col = _status_color(conn["status"])

        pygame.draw.circle(screen, s_col, (dm_x + 14, dm_y + 14), 4)

        hdr = font_terminal.render(conn["name"], True, conn["color"])

        screen.blit(hdr, (dm_x + 26, dm_y + 4))

        st = font_terminal_small.render(

            conn["status"], True, _status_color(conn["status"]),

        )

        screen.blit(st, (dm_x + 26, dm_y + 22))

        pygame.draw.line(

            screen, (30, 50, 60),

            (dm_x + 8, dm_y + 40),

            (dm_x + dm_w - 8, dm_y + 40), 1,

        )

        msg_x = dm_x + 12

        msg_y = dm_y + 48

        msg_w = dm_w - 24

        msg_area_h = dm_h - 116

        history = _dm_history.get(_dm_open_user, [])

        rendered = []

        for m in history:

            text = m["text"]

            is_you = m["from"] == "you"

            col = (220, 220, 220) if is_you else conn["color"]

            words = text.split(" ")

            line = ""

            wrapped = []

            for w in words:

                test = (line + " " + w).strip() if line else w

                if font_terminal_small.size(test)[0] <= msg_w - 60:

                    line = test

                else:

                    if line:

                        wrapped.append(line)

                    line = w

            if line:

                wrapped.append(line)

            for li, ln in enumerate(wrapped):

                prefix = ""

                if li == 0:

                    prefix = "you: " if is_you else f"{conn['name']}: "

                rendered.append((prefix, ln, col, is_you, m["age"]))

        line_h = 16

        max_lines = msg_area_h // line_h

        visible = rendered[-max_lines:]

        for li, (prefix, ln, col, is_you, age) in enumerate(visible):

            ly = msg_y + li * line_h

            alpha = min(255, age * 15)

            if prefix:

                p_col = (140, 140, 145) if is_you else col

                ps = font_terminal_small.render(prefix, True, p_col)

                ps.set_alpha(alpha)

                screen.blit(ps, (msg_x, ly))

                ts = font_terminal_small.render(ln, True, (220, 220, 220) if is_you else (210, 210, 215))

                ts.set_alpha(alpha)

                screen.blit(ts, (msg_x + ps.get_width(), ly))

            else:

                ts = font_terminal_small.render("  " + ln, True, (210, 210, 215))

                ts.set_alpha(alpha)

                screen.blit(ts, (msg_x, ly))

        if _dm_response_delay > 0 and _dm_pending_reply == _dm_open_user:

            dots = "." * (((pygame.time.get_ticks() // 300) % 3) + 1)

            typing = font_terminal_small.render(

                f"{conn['name']} is typing{dots}", True, (100, 130, 150),

            )

            screen.blit(typing, (msg_x, dm_y + dm_h - 64))

        input_box_y = dm_y + dm_h - 42

        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (15, 22, 28), (dm_x + 8, input_box_y, dm_w - 16, 32))

        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (50, 80, 100), (dm_x + 8, input_box_y, dm_w - 16, 32), 1)

        cursor = "_" if (pygame.time.get_ticks() // 500) % 2 == 0 else " "

        input_display = _dm_input + cursor

        if not _dm_input:

            input_display = "Type a message..."

            in_col = (90, 100, 110)

        else:

            in_col = C_WHITE

        ins = font_terminal_small.render(input_display, True, in_col)

        screen.blit(ins, (dm_x + 16, input_box_y + 10))

        send_hint = font_terminal_small.render(

            "[ENTER] send  \u00b7  [ESC] close DM",

            True, (90, 110, 120),

        )

        screen.blit(send_hint, (dm_x + 12, dm_y + dm_h + 4))

def scroll_server_list(direction):

    """direction: +1 scrolls down, -1 scrolls up."""

    global _scroll_offset

    # Scroll by a whole window: stopping at len-1 used to leave a single
    # row stranded on screen.

    max_offset = max(0, len(server_list) - SERVER_VISIBLE_ROWS)

    _scroll_offset = max(0, min(max_offset, _scroll_offset + direction))

def scroll_dm_list(direction):

    global _dm_scroll_offset

    list_bottom_limit = SERVER_LIST_LIMIT

    list_y = CONTACTS_Y

    row_h = CONNECTIONS_ROW_H

    visible_friends = (list_bottom_limit - list_y) // row_h

    max_offset = max(0, len(CONNECTIONS) - visible_friends)

    _dm_scroll_offset = max(0, min(max_offset, _dm_scroll_offset + direction))

# ── KRAPNET relay (real backend) ──────────────────────────────────
# The fictional server_list above is the offline fallback. When a relay
# client is running, its rows replace server_list in-place (same 4-tuple
# shape) so every existing render and hit-test site keeps working with no
# changes. _relay_rules mirrors the master's rules side-table and takes
# priority over SERVER_RULES in the hover tooltip.
#
# Mutable-state discipline: _relay_client / _relay_status / _relay_error
# are owned by THIS module. Anything else that needs them must use
# `import ui.mp as _o` and read `_o.name` -- never `from ui.mp import ...`,
# which would snapshot a stale value.
_relay_client = None
_relay_status = "offline"
_relay_error = ""
_relay_rules = {}
_relay_host = "127.0.0.1"
_relay_port = 27015
_relay_nick = "operator"
# Chat input line. While a live relay is up this is real text the player
# types; it is never populated while offline.
_chat_input = ""
_CHAT_MAX_INPUT = 180
# Default port used when a pasted address omits ":port". Defined here (not
# at the use site) because relay_connect_to() below reads it.
_P_DEFAULT_PORT = 27015

# ── Direct connect ("join by address") ───────────────────────────
# A friend running tools/mp_host.py (or the hosted EXE) gives you an
# address like 1.2.3.4:27015. This is the box you paste it into.
_connect_input = ""
_CONNECT_MAX_INPUT = 60
_connect_rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 300, 26)
_connect_btn_rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 92, 26)
_connect_focused = False
_connect_msg = ""
_connect_msg_age = 0


def connect_bar_take_focus():
    """Called on click so typing goes to the address box, not the game."""
    global _connect_focused
    _connect_focused = True


def connect_bar_click(mouse_pos):
    """Handle a click in the direct-connect row. Returns True if consumed."""
    global _connect_focused
    if _connect_btn_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos):
        return do_direct_connect()
    if _connect_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos):
        _connect_focused = True
        return True
    _connect_focused = False
    return False


def do_direct_connect():
    """Connect to whatever is in the address box. Returns True if we tried."""
    global _connect_msg, _connect_msg_age
    _connect_focused = False
    ok, message = relay_connect_to(_connect_input)
    if ok:
        _connect_msg = "connecting to %s" % message
        audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.3)
    else:
        _connect_msg = message
    _connect_msg_age = 0
    return ok


def direct_connect_key(event):
    """Handle one KEYDOWN for the address box. True if consumed."""
    global _connect_input, _connect_focused
    if not _connect_focused:
        return False
    if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN or event.key == pygame.K_KP_ENTER:
        return do_direct_connect()
    if event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE:
        _connect_input = _connect_input[:-1]
        return True
    if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
        _connect_focused = False
        return True
    # A paste is a TEXTINPUT event, not a keypress; grab the clipboard.
    if event.key == pygame.K_v and (
            event.mod & (pygame.KMOD_CTRL | pygame.KMOD_META)):
        paste = clipboard_text(_CONNECT_MAX_INPUT - len(_connect_input))
        if paste:
            _connect_input += paste
        return True
    if getattr(event, "unicode", "") and event.unicode.isprintable():
        if len(_connect_input) < _CONNECT_MAX_INPUT:
            _connect_input += event.unicode
        return True
    return False


def direct_connect_tick():
    """Age the status message so it fades like the chat lines do."""
    global _connect_msg_age
    _connect_msg_age += 1

# Set True to fall back to the fictional list if the relay is unreachable.
_relay_optional = True


def relay_host():
    """Current master host/port, read from the environment if present.

    Env vars let a player point the game at someone else's master without
    editing code, and let the smoke test spin up a throwaway instance.
    """
    import os
    host = os.environ.get("ACA_MP_HOST", _relay_host)
    try:
        port = int(os.environ.get("ACA_MP_PORT", _relay_port))
    except ValueError:
        port = _relay_port
    return host, port


def relay_start(nick=None, host=None, port=None, discover=True):
    """Start (or restart) the relay client. Safe to call every frame.

    Returns True if a client is running. Never blocks *for long*: start()
    only spawns a daemon thread, and all socket work happens on that
    thread. The optional LAN discovery probe is the one exception -- it is
    a single UDP broadcast with a short timeout, and only runs when no
    explicit host was passed.
    """
    global _relay_client, _relay_nick, _relay_host, _relay_port
    from net.client import MPRelayClient, register_chat_sink

    if nick:
        _relay_nick = nick
    h, p = relay_host()
    if host is not None:
        h = host
    if port is not None:
        p = port
    # Only auto-discover when the caller did not name a host explicitly.
    # An explicit host is a deliberate choice and must not be overridden.
    if discover and host is None:
        try:
            from net.discovery import discover_master
            found = discover_master(timeout=1.0)
            if found:
                h, p = found
        except Exception:
            pass  # discovery is a convenience, never a requirement
    _relay_host, _relay_port = h, p

    if _relay_client is not None:
        _relay_client.host = h
        _relay_client.port = p
        return True

    # Register the sink before starting so no early chat line is dropped.
    register_chat_sink(_on_relay_chat)
    _relay_client = MPRelayClient(host=h, port=p, nickname=_relay_nick,
                                 chat_enabled=True)
    _relay_client.start()
    _relay_client.request_connect()
    return True


def relay_send_chat_line():

    """Send whatever is in the chat input box, then clear it.

    Returns True if a line was actually sent. Echo is handled by the master,
    so we do not append locally -- that would double every message.
    """
    global _chat_input

    text = _chat_input.strip()

    if not text:
        return False

    if not relay_send_chat(text):
        return False

    _chat_input = ""

    return True


def relay_chat_key(event):

    """Handle one KEYDOWN for the chat input. Returns True if consumed.

    Only ENTER and BACKSPACE are claimed here; ordinary character keys are
    consumed too, but only while a live relay is connected. Returning
    True tells the caller to swallow the event so it does not also reach
    the DM composer or the mission input layer.
    """
    global _chat_input

    if not relay_is_live():
        return False

    if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN or event.key == pygame.K_KP_ENTER:
        relay_send_chat_line()
        return True

    if event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE:
        _chat_input = _chat_input[:-1]
        return True

    # A paste is a TEXTINPUT event, not a keypress; grab the clipboard.
    if event.key == pygame.K_v and (
            event.mod & (pygame.KMOD_CTRL | pygame.KMOD_META)):
        paste = clipboard_text(_CHAT_MAX_INPUT - len(_chat_input))
        if paste:
            _chat_input += paste
        return True

    # Printable characters only. Without the isprintable() guard, control
    # codes and dead keys would land in the input box.
    if getattr(event, "unicode", "") and event.unicode.isprintable():
        if len(_chat_input) < _CHAT_MAX_INPUT:
            _chat_input += event.unicode
        return True

    return False


def relay_connect_to(address, nick=None, timeout_note=True):
    """Point the relay at an explicit address and start connecting.

    ``address`` is "host" or "host:port" (IPv4). This is the path a player
    takes when a friend hands them an address, so it must never raise on
    bad input -- it returns (ok, message) instead.

    Passing a host explicitly also disables LAN discovery for this
    connection: an address a friend gave us is a deliberate choice and
    must not be silently replaced by whatever beacon answers.
    """
    if not isinstance(address, str):
        return (False, "bad address")
    text = address.strip()
    if not text:
        return (False, "enter an address")
    # Accept "host:port" and bare "host" (default port).
    if ":" in text:
        host, _sep, port_text = text.rpartition(":")
        try:
            port = int(port_text)
        except ValueError:
            return (False, "port must be a number")
        if not (1 <= port <= 65535):
            return (False, "port out of range")
    else:
        host, port = text, _P_DEFAULT_PORT
    host = host.strip()
    if not host:
        return (False, "missing host")
    # Disallow whitespace and slashes: they cannot appear in a hostname or
    # IPv4 literal, so their presence means a paste accident.
    if any(c.isspace() or c in "/\\?#" for c in host):
        return (False, "address looks malformed")
    relay_start(nick=nick, host=host, port=port, discover=False)
    return (True, "%s:%d" % (host, port))


def relay_stop():
    """Shut the relay client down. Safe when it was never started."""
    global _relay_client, _relay_status, _relay_error
    if _relay_client is not None:
        _relay_client.stop()
        _relay_client = None
    _relay_status = "offline"
    _relay_error = ""
    _set_fixedstep(False)


def _set_fixedstep(on):
    """Turn the multiplayer fixed-timestep accumulator on or off.

    The host simulates the authoritative world, so its simulation rate must
    not depend on its hardware -- otherwise a host that renders slowly hands
    out measurably different fire rates and enemy reactions to every client.
    Advancing the sim in fixed 1/60 ticks removes that dependency.

    Single-player is deliberately untouched: this stays off unless a relay
    session is live, and is forced off on disconnect so a lobby can never
    leave the campaign running on the multiplayer timing path.
    """
    try:
        from core import fixedstep
        fixedstep.set_enabled(bool(on))
    except Exception:
        # A missing/broken fixedstep module must never take the lobby or the
        # game down; multiplayer just runs on legacy timing instead.
        pass


def relay_send_chat(text):
    """Send a chat line to the master. False if offline or rejected."""
    if _relay_client is None:
        return False
    return _relay_client.send_chat(text)


def relay_refresh():
    if _relay_client is None:
        return False
    _relay_client.refresh()
    return True


def _on_relay_chat(msg):
    """Inbound chat sink. Runs on the NETWORK thread, not the render thread.

    Appending to _chat_messages is atomic under the GIL and the list is
    only appended to here, so the renderer iterating it cannot see a
    half-written dict.
    """
    text = msg.get("text")
    user = msg.get("user")
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not isinstance(user, str):
        return
    color = msg.get("color")
    if not (isinstance(color, (list, tuple)) and len(color) == 3):
        color = (180, 180, 180)
    try:
        color = tuple(max(0, min(255, int(c))) for c in color)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        color = (180, 180, 180)
    _chat_messages.append({
        "user": user[:32],
        "text": text[:200],
        "color": color,
        "age": 0,
    })
    if len(_chat_messages) > 50:
        del _chat_messages[:-50]


def relay_status():
    """(status, error) for the UI to display."""
    return _relay_status, _relay_error


def relay_is_live():
    """True when the master answered and we are showing real rows."""
    return _relay_status == "online" and bool(_relay_client)


def _sync_relay_into_server_list():
    """Copy the relay snapshot into the module-level server_list.

    Done in place (slice assignment) so that `import ui.mp as _o; _o.server_list`
    observers see the update -- rebinding the name would leave those
    references pointing at the stale fictional list.
    """
    global _relay_status, _relay_error, _relay_rules
    if _relay_client is None:
        _relay_status = "offline"
        return

    status, error, servers, _nick = _relay_client.state()
    _was_live = _relay_status == "online"
    _relay_status = status
    _relay_error = error

    # Soft notes from the master ("sending too fast", "registering too often")
    # go into the chat panel as system lines. They are not faults and not
    # chat, but the chat panel is where a person looking at this screen would
    # look for an explanation of why their line did not appear.
    for note in _relay_client.take_notes():
        if not note:
            continue
        _chat_messages.append({
            "user": "SYSTEM", "text": note, "color": (240, 200, 110),
            "age": 0,
        })
        if len(_chat_messages) > 50:
            del _chat_messages[:-50]

    # Keep the fixed-timestep switch in step with the session. It goes on
    # only on the offline->online edge (so it is not re-set every frame) and
    # off as soon as we lose the session, which is what stops a lobby from
    # ever leaving the campaign running on multiplayer timing.
    if status == "online" and not _was_live:
        _set_fixedstep(True)
    elif status != "online" and _was_live:
        _set_fixedstep(False)

    if status != "online":
        # Do not clobber the last good list on a blip; the UI keeps showing
        # the fictional rows and the status line explains why.
        return

    if not servers:
        # Connected, but the master is genuinely empty -- show that rather
        # than silently falling back to the fiction.
        server_list[:] = []
        return

    server_list[:] = [(name, cur, mx, ping) for (name, cur, mx, ping, _r) in servers]
    _relay_rules = dict(
        (name, list(lines)) for (name, _c, _m, _p, lines) in servers if lines
    )

    # The fictional chat pool runs until the relay first comes online, so
    # its lines can be sitting in the panel. Drop exactly those the moment
    # we go live -- but ONLY those. The master backfills recent chat to
    # every joiner, and that backfill typically lands in the same breath as
    # the server list, so a blanket clear() would wipe real messages the
    # instant they arrived. Fiction entries are tagged "fict": True at
    # creation precisely so this can tell them apart.
    if not _was_live:
        _chat_messages[:] = [m for m in _chat_messages if not m.get("fict")]


def server_rules_for(name):
    """Rules for a server: relay-provided first, then the local fiction."""
    rules = _relay_rules.get(name)
    if rules:
        return rules
    return SERVER_RULES.get(name)


def trigger_server_refresh():

    global _refresh_active, _refresh_progress

    # With a live relay, ask the master for a fresh list instead of faking
    # one. The client re-queries and _sync_relay_into_server_list picks the
    # answer up on the next frame.

    if relay_refresh():

        audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.4)

        return

    if not _refresh_active:

        _refresh_active = True

        _refresh_progress = 0.0

        audio.play("menu_click", volume=0.4)

def get_kick_message_for_server(server_name):

    if server_name in KICK_MESSAGES_BY_SERVER:

        return _rng_legacy.choice(KICK_MESSAGES_BY_SERVER[server_name])

    return _rng_legacy.choice(KICK_MESSAGES)

def _wrap_server_name(name, font, max_width, max_lines=2):

    """Wrap a server name into up to max_lines lines.

    Returns a list of rendered strings (1 or 2 elements)."""

    if font.size(name)[0] <= max_width:

        return [name]

    words = name.split(" ")

    if len(words) > 1:

        best_split = 1

        for i in range(1, len(words)):

            first = " ".join(words[:i])

            if font.size(first)[0] <= max_width:

                best_split = i

            else:

                break

        line1 = " ".join(words[:best_split])

        line2 = " ".join(words[best_split:])

        if font.size(line2)[0] > max_width:

            ellipsis = "..."

            while line2 and font.size(line2 + ellipsis)[0] > max_width:

                line2 = line2[:-1]

            line2 = line2 + ellipsis

        return [line1, line2]

    mid = len(name) // 2

    while mid > 1 and font.size(name[:mid])[0] > max_width:

        mid -= 1

    line1 = name[:mid]

    line2 = name[mid:]

    if font.size(line2)[0] > max_width:

        ellipsis = "..."

        while line2 and font.size(line2 + ellipsis)[0] > max_width:

            line2 = line2[:-1]

        line2 = line2 + ellipsis

    return [line1, line2]

def server_row_layouts(scroll_offset=None):

    """Row geometry for the server list - the single source of truth.

    Returns [(index, name_lines, row_h, y), ...] for the rows that
    actually fit between SERVER_LIST_TOP and SERVER_LIST_LIMIT.

    The clip is what stops the list from running into the footer
    again whatever the font metrics happen to be.  Both
    draw_server_browser() and the click handler in app.py consume
    this, so the hit boxes can never drift from what is drawn."""

    if scroll_offset is None:

        scroll_offset = _scroll_offset

    layouts = []

    cur_y = SERVER_LIST_TOP

    for vi in range(SERVER_VISIBLE_ROWS):

        i = vi + scroll_offset

        if i >= len(server_list):

            break

        name = server_list[i][0]

        name_lines = _wrap_server_name(name, font_terminal, SERVER_NAME_MAX_W)

        row_h = SERVER_ROW_H_DOUBLE if len(name_lines) > 1 else SERVER_ROW_H_SINGLE

        if cur_y + row_h > SERVER_LIST_LIMIT:

            break

        layouts.append((i, name_lines, row_h, cur_y))

        cur_y += row_h + SERVER_ROW_GAP

    return layouts

def server_region(idx):

    """Stable fake relay region for a server (shown in the tooltip)."""

    name = server_list[idx][0]

    return SERVER_REGIONS[(sum(ord(c) for c in name) + idx) % len(SERVER_REGIONS)]

def enter_arena_hit(mouse_pos):
    """True if the mouse is on the ARENA MATCH button on the browser.

    Lives here rather than in match_screen so the button sits with the rest
    of the browser chrome. The rect is computed rather than cached because
    the panel moves with the window and a stale rect is a button that
    silently does nothing. draw_server_browser() draws the button at these
    exact coordinates -- keep the two in step.
    """
    return enter_arena_rect().collidepoint(mouse_pos)


def enter_arena_rect():
    return pygame.Rect(SERVER_PANEL_X + SERVER_PANEL_W - 286, SERVER_PANEL_Y + 30, 258, 48)


def enter_arena_click(mouse_pos):
    return enter_arena_hit(mouse_pos)


_ARENA_FONT = None


def _arena_font():
    """Cached button font.

    Building a pygame Font every frame is a real cost, and this draws on
    the multiplayer screen where frame time is visible to the player.
    """
    global _ARENA_FONT
    if _ARENA_FONT is None:
        try:
            _ARENA_FONT = pygame.font.Font(None, 16)
        except Exception:
            _ARENA_FONT = pygame.font.Font(pygame.font.get_default_font(), 12)
    return _ARENA_FONT


def draw_server_browser(selected_idx, connecting, kicked_msg, connect_progress=0.0):

    # Operations shell; list/chat/relay presentation below retains its live data.
    _mp_style.background(screen)
    _mp_style.browser_shell(screen, pygame.Rect(SERVER_PANEL_X, SERVER_PANEL_Y,
                                               SERVER_PANEL_W, SERVER_PANEL_H))

    # Give the relay state its own line; keep address entry, connect and
    # refresh together on the row below so the browser header does not read as
    # one cramped run of title, status and controls.
    _bar_y = SERVER_CONNECT_Y
    _connect_btn_rect.w = 92
    _connect_btn_rect.h = 26
    _connect_btn_rect.x = refresh_btn_rect.x - 12 - _connect_btn_rect.w
    _connect_btn_rect.y = _bar_y
    _connect_rect.x = SERVER_PANEL_X + 28
    _connect_rect.w = _connect_btn_rect.x - 10 - _connect_rect.x
    _connect_rect.h = 26
    _connect_rect.y = _bar_y
    refresh_btn_rect.y = _bar_y

    # The subtitle doubles as the connection indicator. When a relay is
    # running it reports the real state (and the real error, e.g. "no master
    # on that host") instead of implying a live KRAPNET that isn't there.

    _rel_st, _rel_err = relay_status()

    # Cached once per frame: the chat panel below branches on it.

    _relay_live = (_rel_st == "online")

    if _rel_st == "online":

        _sub_text = f"KRAPNET  ·  {_relay_host}:{_relay_port}  ·  {len(server_list)} servers online"

        _sub_col = (95, 125, 145)

    elif _rel_st in ("connecting", "error"):

        _sub_text = f"KRAPNET  ·  {_rel_st.upper()}  ·  {_rel_err or 'no master'}"

        _sub_col = (220, 150, 60) if _rel_st == "connecting" else (220, 90, 75)

    else:
